findings.bug: A page token of just "-" (or "--") reaches the range branch, where part.split("-") returns a length-0 array, so rangeParts[0] throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of being handled.
findings.why_real: Verified in a JVM: "-".split("-") has length 0 (trailing empty strings are stripped by String.split with the default limit). The catch clause on line 822 only catches NumberFormatException, so the AIOOBE from rangeParts[0] escapes. The public entry parsePageList(String) (line 636) only catches NumberFormatException too, so it also propagates to the caller, breaking the class's own contract of gracefully returning List.of(1) for bad input.
findings.how_to_prove: GeneralUtils.parsePageList("-", 10, false) -> expected List.of(1) (per the NumberFormatException fallback contract) or a valid page list; actual throws java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Directly: handlePart("-", 10, 0) throws AIOOBE.

findings.bug: Any page token containing 'n' that is not a valid n-expression (e.g. "nx", "n)") makes handlePart call evaluateNFunc, which throws IllegalArgumentException on a failed format check; handlePart does not catch it, so it escapes uncaught.
findings.why_real: evaluateNFunc (lines 700-705) throws IllegalArgumentException when the expression fails the math-expression regex; handlePart's n-branch (lines 801-807) invokes it with no try/catch, and the outer parsePageList(String) (line 642) catches only NumberFormatException, so an invalid page string produces an uncaught IllegalArgumentException instead of the intended List.of(1) fallback. The same escape occurs when totalPages > 10000, because evaluateNFunc rejects maxValue > 10000 (line 692).
findings.how_to_prove: GeneralUtils.parsePageList("nx", 10, false) -> expected graceful fallback List.of(1); actual throws java.lang.IllegalArgumentException("Invalid expression format: nx").

findings.bug: getInstance(processType, liveUpdates) memoizes the executor via computeIfAbsent keyed only on processType, so the liveUpdates flag is captured only on the first call; later calls with a different liveUpdates value silently reuse the original setting.
findings.why_real: computeIfAbsent(processType, ...) (line 52) only runs the mapping function on first insertion, and liveUpdates is read inside that lambda. A second call getInstance(TESSERACT, false) after getInstance(TESSERACT, true) returns the cached instance with liveUpdates=true, contradicting the caller's requested value.
findings.how_to_prove: Call getInstance(Processes.TESSERACT, true) then getInstance(Processes.TESSERACT, false); expected an executor honoring liveUpdates=false, actual returns the same instance with liveUpdates=true (observable via a getter or by verifying identical object reference while the flag differs).
